name: Almond butter
tagline: Slow-roasted almonds ground into a pale, mellow, lightly sweet butter.
metaDescription: Almond butter made from roasted almonds with a pinch of salt. Mellow, nutty and spreadable, lovely on toast, in porridge and in baking.
description: Roasted almonds, ground slowly and patiently, with a pinch of salt: that is this butter. It comes out pale tan, a little looser than peanut butter, and with a gentle, mellow sweetness that suits both breakfast and baking.

The flavour is softer and more rounded than you might expect, with a hint of marzipan on the finish. The texture is smooth with just a trace of grit from the almond skins, which gives it a pleasant, homely feel on the tongue.

Spread it on sourdough with sliced banana, swirl it through porridge, or whisk it into a dressing with lemon and a little water. It melts into brownies and gives cookies a rich, nutty background. A spoonful with a sliced apple is a very easy snack.

Because there are no stabilisers, a little oil may rise to the top of the jar, so stir before using. Looking to make your own? Our guide to homemade nut butter in a food processor shows how, and our raw almonds are a good place to start.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a cool cupboard and stir if oil separates. After opening, keep the lid tight and use within a few months.

name: The big nut hamper
tagline: Five generous bags of roasted and raw nuts in a proper wicker-style hamper.
metaDescription: A generous hamper of dry-roasted almonds, salted cashews, raw walnut halves, honey-roasted peanuts and maple-glazed pecans, gift-ready.
description: When a small box would feel a bit modest, this is the one to send. The big nut hamper holds five full-size bags, packed snugly into a sturdy basket-style box with shredded paper to keep everything in place.

There is something for every type of nut fan. Dry-roasted almonds and salted roasted cashews cover the savoury side, honey-roasted peanuts and maple-glazed pecans bring the sweet, and raw walnut halves are there for the baker in the family.

It suits a family at a holiday, a team after a big project, or a host who has everything. Because the bags are full size, the hamper keeps giving: the snacking goes on for weeks, and the walnuts are ready for the next banana bread.
We pack the hamper to order and add a blank card for your message. If a recipient has a nut allergy, the label has the full allergen details, so it is worth checking before you send.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, sesame and soy.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place. Reseal each bag after opening and keep the walnuts somewhere cool.

name: Breakfast crunch mix
tagline: Oat clusters, almonds, pecans and walnuts for bowls and on-the-go mornings.
metaDescription: A morning mix of honey oat clusters, raw almonds, pecans and walnuts with dried apple and pumpkin seeds. Pour over yoghurt or eat from the bag.
description: This is trail mix for people who do not do trail mix. Golden honey oat clusters carry most of the volume, studded with raw almonds, pecan halves and walnut pieces. It tastes like the best bit of a granola bowl, without needing a bowl.

Dried apple gives soft, mellow sweetness, and pumpkin seeds add a little toasted crunch. The clusters are baked lightly so they stay crisp in milk for a good few minutes, which is exactly the test we use for any breakfast cereal.

Spoon it over yoghurt, stir it into porridge, or sprinkle it over sliced banana. It is also a decent desk-drawer snack for the morning slump. If you are curious about making your own, our homemade granola post walks through the method.
Because the clusters are fragile, we pack this mix gently. A few crumbs at the bottom of the bag are normal, and they make a great topping for anything creamy.
ingredients: Oat clusters (oats, honey, sunflower oil, sugar), raw almonds, raw pecan halves, raw walnut pieces, dried apple, pumpkin seeds.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts, milk and other cereals containing gluten.
storage: Seal tightly after opening and keep somewhere cool and dry so the clusters stay crisp.

name: Cashew butter
tagline: Ultra-creamy cashew butter, naturally sweet and soft enough to drizzle.
metaDescription: Creamy cashew butter made from roasted cashews and a pinch of salt. Naturally sweet, silky and very spreadable, great for sauces and snacks.
description: Cashews are already the creamiest nut in the bowl, so it is no surprise that cashew butter is the silkiest spread on our shelf. We roast the kernels lightly and grind them until the mixture turns soft, pale and almost pourable.

The flavour is mild and gently sweet, with that buttery cashew note and a pinch of salt in the background. It does not have the sharpness of some other butters, which makes it an easy one to like, especially if you prefer something delicate.

It is wonderful on toast with a drizzle of honey, but it also earns its keep in the kitchen. Loosen it with warm water and lemon for a sauce for noodles, stir a spoonful into curry for body, or use it as a base for a no-bake cheesecake filling.

Because it is so soft, it may separate a little in the jar, and a good stir sorts that out. Fans of the ingredient might enjoy our story on where cashews come from, and anyone curious about homemade versions can read our food-processor guide.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a cool cupboard and stir before use. Keep refrigerated after opening if your kitchen is warm, and use within a few months.

name: Chilli lime cashews
tagline: Roasted cashews with a zesty lime kick and a slow-building chilli heat.
metaDescription: Roasted cashews seasoned with lime and chilli. Zesty, warming and crunchy, a lively snack with plenty of personality for any bowl.
description: These cashews arrive with a bright, sharp hit of lime, followed a second later by a gentle chilli warmth that builds without taking over. Underneath it all, the roasted cashew keeps things buttery and round.

We season them after roasting so the flavours stay fresh. The lime gives a tangy lift, the chilli adds slow heat, and a little salt ties it together. They sit somewhere around a medium level of spice, so most people will find them lively rather than painful.

They are great beside a cold drink, but also very good in cooking. Scatter over a mango salad, a coconut curry or a bowl of rice noodles, or crush them over avocado on toast. A small handful can liven up a boring lunch.

We kept the ingredient list short and the flavour direct. If you prefer a gentler snack, try our salted roasted cashews or the plain raw ones. For readers curious about the cashew itself, our where cashews come from post tells the story from tree to bag.
ingredients: Cashews, sunflower oil, sea salt, lime powder, chilli powder, sugar, citric acid.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry cupboard away from light. Eat within a couple of months of opening.

name: Chocolate orchard mix
tagline: Almonds, hazelnuts and pecans with dark chocolate drops and dried apple.
metaDescription: A dessert-leaning snack mix of raw almonds, hazelnuts and pecans with dark chocolate drops, dried apple and raisins. Rich, fruity and not too sweet.
description: Think of an autumn orchard with a chocolatier next door. Raw almonds, hazelnuts and pecan halves provide the base, and small dark chocolate drops melt into the gaps between them. Hazelnut and chocolate is a classic pairing for a reason.

Slices of dried apple add a soft, slightly tart chew, and a few raisins deepen the sweetness without turning it sugary. The chocolate is dark rather than milky, so the finish stays rich and a little bitter, the way a good square of chocolate should.

This mix is happiest as an after-dinner nibble, a gift for a chocolate fan, or a topping for vanilla ice cream. It also bakes well: fold a few handfuls into a cookie dough and skip the extra chocolate chips.
In warm weather the chocolate can soften, so keep the bag somewhere cool. If the drops turn pale on the surface, it is only cocoa butter that has moved, and they still taste fine.
ingredients: Raw almonds, raw hazelnuts, raw pecan halves, dark chocolate drops (cocoa mass, sugar, cocoa butter, emulsifier: soya lecithin), dried apple, raisins.
mayContain: May contain traces of milk, other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place away from sunlight and heat so the chocolate keeps its shape.

name: Chopped walnuts
tagline: Ready-chopped walnut pieces for banana bread, brownies and salads.
metaDescription: Fresh chopped walnut pieces for baking and cooking. Add to banana bread, brownies, salads and porridge. No chopping board required.
description: Walnuts are the nut of banana bread and brownies, and these pieces save you the job of chopping. We shell and chop them to an even size, roughly the size of a lentil to a chickpea, so they spread nicely through batter.

The flavour is earthy and slightly bitter, with a soft, buttery crunch. That edge is a good match for sweet things like bananas, maple and dark chocolate, and it holds up well alongside strong cheeses and bitter leaves in a salad.

Toast them for five minutes in a dry pan before baking to wake up the oils and deepen the taste. You can also stir them into porridge, scatter them over roasted vegetables, or blitz them into a rough pesto with garlic and olive oil.

Walnuts are fragile and their oils can turn if they are stored badly, so we pack them in small quantities and recommend using them within a couple of months. Our walnut banana bread recipe is a good place to start.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store sealed in the fridge or freezer for best freshness. Away from strong smells.

name: Classic trail mix
tagline: Almonds, cashews, peanuts and raisins: the mix that started every hike.
metaDescription: A balanced everyday trail mix of roasted almonds, salted cashews, honey-roasted peanuts, raisins and sunflower seeds, packed fresh to order.
description: This is the mix we reach for when someone says they just want a proper trail mix and nothing fancy. Dry-roasted almonds bring the crunch, salted roasted cashews add a buttery softness, and honey-roasted peanuts give a sweet, sticky edge that keeps every handful interesting.

Plump raisins and sunflower seeds fill the gaps. The raisins are chewy and sweet, which stops the salt from taking over, and the seeds add a light, nutty snap. We blend the mix by hand in small batches so the ratio stays generous with the nuts instead of the fruit.

It travels well in a jacket pocket, sits happily in a desk drawer, and works as a topping for yoghurt or porridge when you want some texture. If you like to tweak, pour it into a bowl and add a few chocolate chips or dried cherries of your own.
Our guide to building a trail mix explains how we think about the balance of salty, sweet and crunchy, if you want to make your own blend at home.
ingredients: Dry-roasted almonds, salted roasted cashews, honey-roasted peanuts (peanuts, honey, sugar), raisins, sunflower seeds.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, sesame and soy.
storage: Keep in a cool, dry place in a resealable bag or jar. Best eaten within a couple of months of opening.

name: Crunchy peanut butter
tagline: Thick roasted peanut butter packed with chunky, crunchy peanut pieces.
metaDescription: Crunchy peanut butter with roasted peanut pieces in every spoonful. A thick, hearty spread for toast, sandwiches and baking.
description: For people who think peanut butter should have something to chew, this is the jar. We grind roasted peanuts into a thick base, then fold in a generous scoop of coarsely chopped peanuts so every spoonful has texture.

The flavour is deep and toasty, with a pinch of salt and nothing else added. The crunch comes from real nut pieces, not from fillers, so it softens a little as it sits on warm toast and stays satisfying on a cold cracker.

It is a hardy spread that stands up to heavier jobs. Stir it into porridge, spread it thickly on a banana, layer it into a sandwich with jam, or melt a spoonful into a stir-fry sauce. In baking, it makes biscuits and bars with a more rustic bite.

As with any natural peanut butter, you may see some oil on the surface, so give it a stir when you open it. It contains peanuts, so check the label carefully if you or anyone you cook for has an allergy. Prefer a silkier texture? Reach for our smooth peanut butter instead.
mayContain: May contain traces of tree nuts.
storage: Store in a cool cupboard. Stir well if oil separates. Keep the lid tight after opening and use within a few months.

name: Dry-roasted almonds
tagline: Slow-roasted almonds with a deep golden crunch and no added oil or salt.
metaDescription: Dry-roasted almonds with no oil or salt added. Deeply golden, extra crunchy and toasty, a simple snack for the desk, bag or bowl.
description: We roast these almonds in dry heat only, with no oil and no salt, until the kernels turn deep golden and the whole thing smells like a bakery. The result is a louder, toastier almond than the raw version, with a snappy crunch that lasts.

Roasting concentrates the flavour and dries the nut slightly, which is why it feels crisper between the teeth. You can taste a hint of caramel from the browning reaction, plus that familiar warmth you get from toast. Because nothing is added, they stay clean and simple.

They are a handy snack for a desk drawer or a coat pocket, but they also work in the kitchen. Chop them onto yoghurt, stir them through a grain salad, or crush them over roasted vegetables for texture. Sweet and savoury dishes both like them.

If you want to see how this is done at home, our how to roast almonds at home guide explains the timing. Prefer something with a little more attitude? The smoked almonds start from the same nut but take it in a smokier direction.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in an airtight tin or jar away from heat and light. Eat within a couple of months of opening.

name: The festive nut collection
tagline: Nuts in the shell spirit: pecans, Brazils, hazelnuts, walnuts and peanuts.
metaDescription: A seasonal gift box of maple-glazed pecans, raw Brazil nuts, hazelnuts, walnut halves and honey-roasted peanuts. Bring on the bowl and the nutcracker.
description: This box is for the table at the end of a big meal. It gathers the nuts people have always put in a bowl at holiday time: sticky maple-glazed pecans, raw Brazil nuts, raw hazelnuts, raw walnut halves and honey-roasted peanuts.

Brazil nuts are large and creamy, hazelnuts are sweet and crisp, and walnuts have a gentle bitterness that works well with cheese. The glazed pecans and honey peanuts add a bit of sparkle for anyone with a sweet tooth.

We pack everything into a deep red box with a ribbon and a card for your message. Put the tubs in bowls, add a nutcracker if you like theatre, and let people help themselves. The leftovers are good for baking in the weeks after.
The nuts here are shelled and ready to eat, so no cracking is required unless you want it. The box is a seasonal pick, so we make it in limited batches.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and sesame.
storage: Keep in a cool, dry place. Reseal tubs after use and store walnuts and pecans somewhere cool.

name: Flaked almonds
tagline: Thin, pale almond slivers for topping, toasting and decorating.
metaDescription: Delicate flaked almonds for baking and finishing. Toast for salads, scatter over tarts or press onto cakes for a golden, crisp topping.
description: Flaked almonds are almonds sliced into thin, pale curls. They are light and delicate, which makes them ideal for finishing dishes: a golden scatter over a tart, a crown on a cake, or a crunchy lift for a bowl of porridge.

Raw, they are mild and slightly milky. Toasted, they turn gold and fragrant in a few minutes, and the edges go crisp and nutty. Watch them closely, as the thin slices go from pale to burnt very fast in a hot pan or oven.

They are the traditional topping for Bakewell-style tarts and many Danish pastries, and they work in savoury dishes too. Try them over green beans with butter, in a rice pilaf, or in a creamy chicken dish for a bit of texture.
We slice them ourselves from blanched almonds so the flakes stay whole rather than crumbling to dust. They are packed in a resealable bag to keep them dry and crisp.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in a sealed bag in a cool, dry cupboard. Toast only what you need, just before using.

name: Ground almonds
tagline: Finely milled almonds for cakes, macaroons and frangipane.
metaDescription: Finely ground blanched almonds for baking. Gives cakes a moist crumb and a gentle nutty sweetness. Use in frangipane, macaroons and more.
description: Ground almonds are the quiet hero of the baking cupboard. Ours are blanched, so the skins are removed, then milled to a fine, pale, slightly sandy powder. The result is mild, sweet and creamy, and it blends invisibly into batters.

In cakes, they keep the crumb moist and tender, and they bring a delicate marzipan note without being overpowering. They are the foundation of frangipane, the classic tart filling, and they are essential for macaroons and many flourless bakes.

You can swap some of the flour in a recipe for ground almonds to add richness, though they behave differently to wheat flour, so start with a small swap. They also thicken curries and sauces, and make a good coating for fish or chicken.

Ground almonds go off faster than whole nuts because more surface is exposed, so we mill in small batches. Our post on almond flour vs ground almonds explains the small but important differences between them.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry place. Once opened, use within a few weeks or store in the fridge.

name: Hazelnut cocoa spread
tagline: A glossy chocolate and hazelnut spread made with plenty of roasted nuts.
metaDescription: Chocolate hazelnut spread with roasted hazelnuts and cocoa. Glossy, rich and nutty, perfect on toast, pancakes, crepes and fruit.
description: This is a proper hazelnut spread with cocoa, not a chocolate spread with a rumour of hazelnut. We roast the nuts until they are fragrant, grind them smooth, and blend them with cocoa and sugar for a glossy, rich, spoonable finish.

The flavour is led by the nut: toasty and slightly sweet, with a deep cocoa note behind it and a trace of milk powder for softness. The texture is silky and thick, easy to spread on warm toast, and pleasantly rich on a spoon.

Use it on pancakes and crepes, sandwich it between biscuits, or swirl it through a bowl of yoghurt. It is also very good with strawberries or banana. A spoonful stirred into hot milk makes a quick hazelnut hot chocolate.

This spread contains hazelnuts and milk, so check the label if you cook for anyone with allergies. If you would like to make your own, start with our raw hazelnuts and follow the guide on how to toast and skin hazelnuts. The same nut makes our hazelnut flour for baking.
ingredients: Roasted hazelnuts (45%), sugar, skimmed milk powder, cocoa powder (8%), sunflower oil, emulsifier (sunflower lecithin), vanilla extract.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts and soy.
storage: Store in a cool, dry cupboard. Do not refrigerate, as it will firm up. Keep the lid closed after opening.

name: Hazelnut flour
tagline: Fine hazelnut meal for cakes, pastry and a nutty crumb.
metaDescription: Finely ground hazelnut flour for baking. Adds a sweet, toasty flavour to cakes, shortbread, pastry and brownies. Pairs well with chocolate.
description: Hazelnut flour is simply hazelnuts ground to a fine meal. It has a warm, sweet, toasty aroma, and it brings a distinctive depth to bakes that ground almonds cannot quite match, especially in anything chocolatey or coffee flavoured.

Use it to replace a portion of the plain flour in shortbread for a sandy, crumbly bite, or fold it into brownies and chocolate cakes for richness. It also works in the base for a tart, where it creates a crisp, fragrant crust.

Because there is no gluten in the nuts, flour made from them behaves differently in a recipe. It will not give structure on its own, so mix it with other flours or eggs. Start by swapping around a quarter of the flour and adjust from there.

We grind small amounts at a time so the oils stay fresh. For extra flavour, toast the flour in a dry pan for a few minutes, stirring often, then let it cool before using it. Our guide to toasting hazelnuts has useful tips.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in a sealed container in the fridge. Ground nuts spoil faster than whole ones.

name: Honey-roasted peanuts
tagline: Peanuts roasted in a sticky honey glaze, sweet first and salty after.
metaDescription: Peanuts roasted with a honey glaze and a pinch of salt. Sweet, sticky and crunchy, a nostalgic snack for the cinema, the car or the sofa.
description: These peanuts are roasted until crunchy and then coated in a thin honey glaze that sets to a shiny, slightly tacky shell. The first taste is sweet and floral, and the salt arrives just afterwards to keep it balanced.

The glaze is only a light coat, so the peanut flavour is still the star. Peanuts have an earthy, roasted character that works well with sweetness, and the contrast with the crisp interior makes the bag disappear faster than you planned.

Think of them as a snack for long journeys, film nights and board games. They are also good chopped over ice cream, stirred into a cookie dough or crushed over a bowl of spiced noodles for a sweet and savoury finish.

Peanuts are technically legumes, which is a fun fact you can read about in our post on whether peanuts are really nuts. They are still a common allergen, so read the label carefully. If you like the idea of a glazed nut but prefer pecans, take a look at our maple-glazed pecans.
ingredients: Peanuts, honey (9%), sugar, sunflower oil, sea salt.
mayContain: May contain traces of tree nuts.
storage: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place so the glaze stays crisp rather than sticky.

name: Maple-glazed pecans
tagline: Pecan halves baked in a maple glaze until they are sticky, crisp and toffee-sweet.
metaDescription: Pecan halves coated in a maple glaze and baked until crisp. Sweet, toasty and sticky, lovely on salads, desserts or by the handful.
description: Take a perfectly buttery pecan, wrap it in a maple glaze and bake it until the coating crisps into a thin, caramel-like shell. That is the whole idea, and it works very well.

The first bite is sweet, with a deep, woody maple flavour and a hint of toffee. Then comes the soft, tender crunch of the pecan underneath, with a faint pinch of salt that stops it from being too sugary. It is more elegant than a candied nut and less fussy than a praline.

They are a natural for the cheese board, and they make a quick upgrade to a green salad with goat's cheese and pear. Sprinkle them over porridge, ice cream or a stack of pancakes, or chop them into a loaf cake. They are also dangerously good straight from the bag.

If you would like to try the technique yourself, our maple-glazed pecans at home post walks through it. For something plainer, our raw pecan halves give you the same nut with no coating, and a blank canvas for pecan pie bars.
ingredients: Pecans, sugar, maple syrup (6%), sunflower oil, sea salt.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry spot. Humidity softens the glaze, so reseal promptly.

name: The nut butter trio
tagline: Almond, cashew and pistachio butter in three small jars.
metaDescription: A gift set of three small jars: creamy almond butter, mellow cashew butter and vivid pistachio butter. Spread, stir or eat by the spoon.
description: Three small jars, three very different spreads. Almond butter is toasty and a touch sweet, cashew butter is soft and mellow, and pistachio butter is rich, savoury and unmistakably green. Together they make an easy tasting set.

Each jar is made with nuts and nothing much else, so the flavour is clean and the texture is naturally smooth. A little oil may rise to the top, which is normal and shows there are no stabilisers. Stir it back in and you are ready to go.

Spread them on toast, swirl them into porridge, or whisk a spoonful into a dressing or a sauce. Pistachio butter on warm bread with a pinch of salt is a small joy. Cashew butter turns a smoothie creamy without any fuss.
The jars are small enough to finish in a week or two, so everything stays fresh. Our homemade nut butter post is a good read for anyone who wants to try making a batch themselves.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store unopened in a cool, dry cupboard. After opening, keep in the fridge and stir before use.

name: Pecan pieces
tagline: Buttery pecan pieces, broken just right for pies, bars and cookies.
metaDescription: Sweet, buttery pecan pieces for baking. Ideal for pecan pie bars, cookies, sticky buns and granola. A thrifty way to stock the baking shelf.
description: Pecan pieces are halves that did not quite make it, and that is a good thing for your baking. They cost less than whole halves and spread through batters and fillings more evenly, which is exactly what you want in bars and cookies.

The flavour is sweet, soft and buttery with a faint maple note, and the texture is crisp on the outside and tender in the middle. They toast beautifully, but even straight from the bag they carry a rich, almost caramel taste.
Use them in pecan pie bars, sticky buns, oatmeal cookies or a quick coffee cake. They are also lovely over roasted sweet potatoes, in a carrot salad, or crushed over pancakes with a drizzle of syrup.
Our pecan pie bars recipe uses these pieces and shows how well they hold their shape in a gooey filling. We pack them in small bags and suggest using them within a couple of months.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep sealed in the fridge for best flavour. Cool and dark is fine for short periods.

name: Pine nuts
tagline: Small, creamy, resinous pine nuts for pesto, salads and baking.
metaDescription: Soft, creamy pine nuts for pesto, salads, pilafs and baking. Toast in a dry pan to bring out their sweet, buttery, slightly resinous flavour.
description: Pine nuts are the small, ivory seeds tucked inside pine cones, and they are one of the more expensive nuts to harvest, which is why they come in smaller bags. The reward is a soft, creamy texture and a sweet, slightly resinous flavour.

Raw, they are mild and a little waxy. A couple of minutes in a dry pan turns them golden and brings out a buttery, toasty character. Keep them moving, because they go from pale to scorched in seconds.

The classic use is pesto, where they are blended with basil, garlic, cheese and olive oil. They are equally good scattered over a salad, folded into a rice pilaf with raisins, or baked into biscuits and cakes for a delicate crunch.

Because they are so rich in oil, pine nuts can spoil quickly. We pack them in small quantities and suggest keeping them in the fridge. If they smell sharp or paint-like, it is time to replace them. Our post on why nuts go rancid explains the reason.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store sealed in the fridge or freezer. Use within a couple of months of opening.

name: Pistachio butter
tagline: Vivid green-tinged pistachio butter with a rich, sweet, slightly resinous flavour.
metaDescription: Pistachio butter made from roasted pistachios and a pinch of salt. Rich, creamy and subtly sweet, ideal for toast, desserts and baking.
description: Pistachio butter is the fancy one on the shelf, and it knows it. We roast shelled pistachios gently and grind them into a thick paste that keeps a hint of the nut's green tinge, giving a colour you do not see in other spreads.

The flavour is rich, sweet and a little resinous, with a savoury edge from the pinch of salt that stops it from being cloying. The texture is creamy but slightly looser than a peanut butter, and it gets a few tiny flecks from the nut skins.

Spoon it onto warm toast with a few slices of fig, or swirl it through yoghurt. In baking it works in shortbread, thumbprint biscuits and cakes. Loosened with a bit of cream, it makes an excellent sauce for ice cream or a tart filling.

Pistachios are a premium nut, and this jar reflects that in the price. It is an easy way to add a different flavour to your pantry. As always, check the label for allergens, and stir the jar before use if oil has risen to the surface.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a cool, dark cupboard and stir before use. Keep tightly closed after opening and use within a few months.

name: Raw almonds
tagline: Whole, unroasted almonds with the skins on, ready for baking, soaking or snacking.
metaDescription: Whole raw almonds with their skins on. A pale, crisp, mildly sweet nut for baking, soaking, milling or eating straight from the bag.
description: These are plain, whole almonds in their brown skins, nothing added and nothing done to them. Bite one and you get a firm, pale crunch with a mild, faintly sweet flavour that tastes a bit like marzipan's quiet cousin.

Because they are raw, they are a blank canvas. Toast a handful in a dry pan for a few minutes and the aroma fills the kitchen. Soak them overnight and they soften enough to blend into a creamy homemade milk. Chop them roughly over porridge, or grind them fine for cakes and biscuits.

We sort each batch carefully so you get mostly whole kernels with very few chips. The skins add a little tannic bite and some colour, which suits rustic bakes. If you prefer them blanched, a quick dunk in hot water slips the skins right off.

Keep a bag in the cupboard for the days when you cannot decide what you fancy. They are the sort of ingredient that quietly improves a lot of dinners, from a rice pilaf to a salad that needed something crunchy. See our raw nuts range for more unroasted staples.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a cool, dry, dark place in a resealable container. Use within a few months of opening for the best flavour.

name: Raw Brazil nuts
tagline: Big, creamy Brazil nuts with a rich, milky flavour and a satisfying chew.
metaDescription: Large raw Brazil nuts, shelled and unsalted. Creamy, rich and satisfyingly chewy, good for snacking, chopping and baking.
description: Brazil nuts are the heavyweights of the bowl. Long, pale and generously sized, they have a dense, creamy bite and a rich, milky flavour that feels almost indulgent for something so plain.

Their size makes them easy to spot in a mix, and just as easy to use on their own. Slice them thinly over a salad, chop them for a crumble, or shave them with a vegetable peeler to make curls for desserts. A quick toast in the oven brings out a gentle sweetness.

We pack these shelled and unsalted, with no oils or coatings. Expect a few differences in shape from nut to nut, which is just nature being nature. The texture is firm at first and then almost soft as you chew, quite unlike a crisp almond or a crumbly pecan.

Because Brazil nuts are so oily, they are best bought in modest amounts and eaten within a reasonable time. Our guide to storing nuts so they stay fresh has all the tips you need, and our post on why nuts go rancid explains the science.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dark place. Their high oil content means they are best used within a few months.

name: Raw cashews
tagline: Plump, buttery, ivory cashews with a gentle sweetness and a soft crunch.
metaDescription: Creamy raw cashew kernels, whole and unsalted. Soft in the bite and gently sweet, ideal for sauces, curries, nut milks and snacking.
description: Raw cashews are the soft-spoken member of the nut bowl. They are curved, ivory-coloured and plump, with a slightly yielding crunch and a sweet, buttery flavour that never shouts over the rest of your meal.

That mellow character is exactly why cooks love them. Soak them in warm water and blitz until smooth and you have a rich cream for pasta sauces, soups and dairy-free desserts. Toss them whole into a stir-fry near the end of cooking, or simmer them in a curry where they turn tender and silky.

We buy whole kernels and keep broken pieces to a minimum, so the bag is mostly the good-looking ones. They are unroasted and unsalted, which means you control the seasoning. Fifteen minutes in a hot oven with a pinch of salt gives you a fine bar snack.

Cashews have a higher proportion of starch than many nuts, which is partly why they blend so smoothly. Read more about their origins in our guide to where cashews come from, or pick up a jar of our cashew butter if you want the creamy result without the effort.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in an airtight container somewhere cool and dark. For longer storage, the fridge keeps their delicate oils fresh.

name: Raw hazelnuts
tagline: Round, shelled hazelnuts with the skins on: crisp, sweet and made for toasting.
metaDescription: Shelled raw hazelnuts with skins on. Crisp and mildly sweet, they come alive when toasted. Great for baking, spreads and chocolate.
description: Raw hazelnuts are small, round and firmly crisp, with a clean, faintly sweet flavour that is a little shy until you apply some heat. Shelled and ready to use, they still wear their papery brown skins.

Toasting changes everything. Ten minutes in a medium oven, then a rub in a tea towel to loosen the skins, and the nuts turn deep gold with that unmistakable warm, nutty perfume. From there they can go into cakes, brownies and biscotti, or be ground into a rough meal for tart bases.

Hazelnuts also have a famous affinity for chocolate and coffee, so keep a bag handy if you like making your own spreads or truffles. They hold their crunch in baking better than many softer nuts, and they chop cleanly without turning to dust.

If you have never done the toasting and skinning dance, our step-by-step guide shows how to toast and skin hazelnuts without losing your temper. For a finished product, try the hazelnut cocoa spread, which uses the same nut roasted and blitzed until glossy.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark cupboard. Toasted hazelnuts keep best in the fridge.

name: Raw pecan halves
tagline: Sweet, buttery pecan halves with a tender bite, made for pies and porridge.
metaDescription: Raw pecan halves with a naturally sweet, buttery flavour and a tender texture. Perfect for pies, granola, salads and toasting.
description: Pecans are the sweet tooth of the nut world. Each deep-russet half is ridged and tender, with a buttery flavour that carries hints of maple and toffee even though nothing has been added.

Their soft texture makes them very forgiving. Fold them into cookie dough, press them onto the top of a tart, or crush them for a crumble topping. In savoury cooking they are lovely roasted with sweet potato or tossed into a salad with bitter leaves and a sharp dressing.

This is the raw version, so a few minutes in a dry pan or a warm oven is a good idea if you want a deeper, more toasted taste. Watch them closely, because the same sugars that make them taste so good also make them catch quickly.

We pick halves that are whole and plump rather than shards, which matters if you are decorating something. Looking for a ready-made treat instead? Our maple-glazed pecans are the same nut with a sticky coat, or try the recipe in our pecan pie bars post.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry, dark place. Pecans are rich in oil, so the fridge or freezer helps if you store them for months.

name: Raw walnut halves
tagline: Pale, crinkly walnut halves with a rich flavour and a pleasant bitter edge.
metaDescription: Raw walnut halves with a rich, slightly bitter taste and a tender crunch. Great in baking, salads, porridge and stuffings.
description: Walnut halves look like tiny brains, and they taste far better than that sounds. The flesh is tender and crinkled, with a rich, woody flavour and a pleasant bitter edge from the thin skin that keeps them from being dull.

Use them where you want a bit of grown-up character. They are the classic partner for ripe pears and blue cheese, they turn banana bread into something special, and a handful scattered over roasted beetroot makes a very good lunch. Toast them lightly to bring out their sweetness and soften that bitterness.

We select mostly intact halves in a light amber shade, as darker ones can taste stronger and a little harsher. They are packed raw, so you decide what happens next: bake, chop, crush into a pesto, or simply eat them with a cup of tea.

Walnuts are an oil-rich nut, which makes them one of the more delicate things in the pantry. Keep them sealed and cool, and take a look at our notes on why nuts go rancid if you ever wonder whether a forgotten bag is still good.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store in a sealed container in a cool, dark spot, or the fridge in warm weather. Walnuts turn stale quicker than most nuts.

name: The roaster's selection box
tagline: Five roasted nuts, from plain and smoky to sweet and spicy.
metaDescription: A gift box of five roasted nuts: dry-roasted and smoked almonds, salted and chilli lime cashews, plus maple-glazed pecans. Roasted by us.
description: This box is our roasting room in miniature. Each tub shows a different side of the craft: plain dry-roasted almonds, smoky almonds, salted cashews, chilli lime cashews and sticky maple-glazed pecans.

Putting two almonds and two cashews side by side is the fun part. You taste how the same nut changes with a different roast or seasoning, from clean and toasty to smoky or bright and tangy. The pecans round it off as the sweet finish.

It is a good pick for someone who cooks, hosts or just likes to snack with some thought. Put the tubs out on a board with cheese and fruit and let people compare. It also makes a thoughtful present for anyone who has just bought their first proper oven or air fryer.
Every tub is roasted in small batches and sealed soon after cooling, so the nuts reach the recipient crisp. A card in the box explains what to taste first and what to save for last.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts and sesame.
storage: Keep in a cool, dry, dark place. Close each tub firmly after opening.

name: Salted roasted cashews
tagline: Golden roasted cashews finished with a light dusting of sea salt.
metaDescription: Roasted cashews with a light sprinkle of sea salt. Buttery, golden and moreish, the sort of snack that vanishes from the bowl quickly.
description: This is the cashew most people picture when they think of a bar snack: golden, glossy, buttery and lightly salted. We roast the kernels until they colour and then season them gently, so the sweetness of the nut still comes through.

Roasting gives the cashew a firmer crunch than its raw cousin and a rounder, toastier taste. The salt makes them dangerously easy to eat by the handful, which is why we suggest putting some in a bowl rather than eating from the bag.

Beyond snacking, they are a lovely garnish. Scatter them over a noodle dish, a rice bowl or a bowl of spicy soup for a crunchy finish, or chop them into a slaw. They also sit nicely next to a cold drink at the end of a long day.

Most of the cashews we use are whole kernels, so you get that familiar kidney shape with few broken bits. Check the label if you are watching your salt, and compare with our raw cashews if you want to season them yourself. Want something livelier? Try the chilli lime cashews.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. Reseal the bag after opening so the nuts stay crisp.

name: The small gift box
tagline: Three roasted favourites in a neat little box, ready to hand over.
metaDescription: A compact gift box with dry-roasted almonds, salted roasted cashews and maple-glazed pecans, packed in a kraft box with a tie of twine.
description: Sometimes a gift just needs to say thank you, and this little box does it well. Inside are three tubs of our most popular roasted nuts: dry-roasted almonds, salted roasted cashews and maple-glazed pecans.

The trio covers the bases. The almonds are crunchy and plain, the cashews are salty and soft, and the pecans are sweet and sticky with a hint of maple. Together they make a tidy sampler that suits almost anyone who likes a nibble.

The box is kraft card with a tie of twine and a blank tag for your own message. It slips through a letterbox gap on a good day and sits easily on a desk or a dinner table. Nothing about it needs wrapping. It is also a handy size for a teacher, a neighbour or a colleague who has done you a favour.
Wondering what else to put in a gift? Our guide to building a nut gift box explains how we choose and balance the contents.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Keep in a cool, dry place. Once a tub is opened, reseal it and eat within a few weeks.

name: Smoked almonds
tagline: Roasted almonds with a savoury, barbecue-style smoke flavour and a dark, crunchy finish.
metaDescription: Roasted almonds with a smoky, savoury flavour and a deep brown coat. Bold, crunchy and good with drinks, cheese or a picnic.
description: If a campfire and a cupboard staple ever met, they would make these almonds. They are roasted and finished with a smoky, savoury seasoning that sits on the surface, giving each nut a deep brown coat and a bold first taste.

Underneath the smoke is the same dependable crunch you expect from an almond. The flavour is savoury rather than sweet, with a hint of salt and a faint edge of paprika-style warmth, so they sit comfortably alongside strong cheese, cured meats and cold beer.

They also earn their place in cooking. Crush a few over a bowl of lentils, sprinkle them into a pasta with roasted peppers, or chop them into a salad with sharp leaves. A little goes a long way, so you can season a dish without reaching for the salt shaker.

The smoke flavour comes from the seasoning, not from a long stay in a smokehouse, so the nuts keep their texture. They are one of the most popular snacks in our roasted range, and they make a fine addition to any gift box. Keep them away from sweet bakes and you will be happy.
ingredients: Almonds, sunflower oil, sea salt, smoked paprika, natural smoke flavouring, yeast extract.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts and peanuts.
storage: Store sealed in a cool, dry cupboard away from sunlight. Eat within a couple of months of opening.

name: Smooth peanut butter
tagline: Silky, roasted-peanut butter with just a pinch of salt and nothing else.
metaDescription: Smooth peanut butter made from roasted peanuts and a pinch of salt. Silky, rich and spreadable, great on toast, in sauces and by the spoon.
description: This jar is as simple as peanut butter gets: roasted peanuts, ground until silky, with a pinch of salt. No sweeteners, no stabilisers, just a deep roasted flavour and a texture you can spread on warm toast without tearing it.

Because it is made without added stabilisers, a thin layer of natural oil may rise to the top over time. That is normal, and a good stir brings it back together. After that, the butter is thick, glossy and rich, with the toasty, slightly salty taste of freshly roasted peanuts.

Use it the obvious way, on bread or crackers, or lean on it in the kitchen. A spoonful thickens a satay sauce, enriches a noodle dressing and gives a good chew to cookies. It also pairs nicely with banana, apple slices or a drizzle of honey.

Peanuts are one of the most common food allergens, so read the label carefully. If you like a little crunch, our crunchy peanut butter uses the same recipe with chopped nuts folded in. For a deeper dive on the ingredient, see our post on peanuts and their botanical status.
mayContain: May contain traces of tree nuts.
storage: Store in a cool cupboard. Stir if oil separates. Once opened, keep the lid tightly closed and use within a few months.

name: Spicy snack mix
tagline: Chilli lime cashews, smoked almonds and peanuts with a proper kick.
metaDescription: A savoury, spicy snack mix of chilli lime cashews, smoked almonds, peanuts and pumpkin seeds. No fruit, no sweetness, just heat and salt.
description: No raisins here, and no apologies. This mix is for people who think a snack should wake them up. Chilli lime cashews lead with tangy heat, smoked almonds add a campfire depth, and crunchy peanuts keep things grounded.

Pumpkin seeds toast quickly in the roasting pan, which gives them a nutty, green flavour that cuts through the spice. A pinch of chilli flakes and a little sea salt finish the blend, so the heat builds gently instead of arriving all at once.

It is built for the bar. Tip a bowl out next to a cold drink and it will disappear. It also works crushed lightly over a noodle bowl or tucked into a taco, where the lime and smoke give extra character.
The heat is medium, comfortable for most chilli fans and easy to soften by mixing in a handful of plain nuts. If you like it fiercer, a few extra chilli flakes in the bag do the job.
ingredients: Chilli lime cashews (cashews, sunflower oil, sea salt, chilli, lime flavouring), smoked almonds (almonds, sea salt, smoke flavouring), peanuts, pumpkin seeds, chilli flakes, sea salt.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, sesame and soy.
storage: Keep in a resealable bag in a cool, dry place so the seasoning stays crisp.

name: Summit trail mix
tagline: Four nuts, pumpkin seeds and tart cranberries for the long climb.
metaDescription: A hearty trail mix of dry-roasted almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts and cashews with pumpkin seeds and dried cranberries, built for long days out.
description: Summit is our nut-forward mix, designed for people who want to be chewing something substantial by the time they reach the top. It leads with dry-roasted almonds and raw hazelnuts, adds walnut halves for a gentle bitterness, and rounds things out with creamy cashews.

Pumpkin seeds give a green, toasty crunch, and a small scattering of dried cranberries brings a sharp, tart note so the whole mix does not feel heavy. We keep the fruit to a minimum on purpose. This is a nut mix with a hint of sweetness, not the other way round.
Because it is dense, a small handful goes a long way. It is a good companion for a packed lunch, a long drive or a late meeting, and it holds its texture well in a bag for days at a time.
Walnuts are the most delicate nut in the blend, so we pack the mix in small batches to keep everything tasting fresh when it reaches you.
ingredients: Dry-roasted almonds, raw hazelnuts, raw walnut halves, raw cashews, pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries (cranberries, sugar, sunflower oil).
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts and sesame.
storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry, dark spot. Refrigerate in warm weather to protect the walnuts.

name: The tasting flight box
tagline: Raw, roasted and smoked, side by side. Taste one nut five ways.
metaDescription: A tasting box of five small tubs: raw, dry-roasted and smoked almonds, plus raw and salted roasted cashews. Compare how roasting changes a nut.
description: A flight is a tasting in a row, and this box applies the idea to nuts. Five small tubs let you compare two favourites at different stages: raw, dry-roasted and smoked almonds, and raw and salted roasted cashews.

Start with the raw almonds: pale, mild and a bit milky. Move to the dry-roasted ones for deeper, toastier flavour, then the smoked ones for a savoury finish. With the cashews, notice how salt and heat turn a soft, sweet nut into a very moreish one.

It is a good present for curious eaters, cooks and anyone who has ever asked what the difference between raw and roasted really is. It also works for a dinner party: hand out small plates and let guests score each tub.
A tasting card with a simple order of play is included. For a deeper look at what roasting does to flavour, our raw vs roasted post is a good companion read.
ingredients: See the contents list on the product page.
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts and sesame.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place and reseal each tub after tasting. Enjoy within a few weeks of opening.

name: Tropical trail mix
tagline: Cashews and almonds with dried mango, pineapple and banana chips.
metaDescription: A sunny trail mix of raw cashews and almonds with chewy dried mango, pineapple and crisp banana chips. Sweet, fruity and easy to snack on.
description: If a beach holiday were a snack, it would look a lot like this. We start with creamy raw cashews and lightly crunchy almonds, then fold in strips of chewy dried mango and sticky pineapple pieces for a bright, sweet tang.

Crisp banana chips run through the middle for a bit of crackle. They soften slightly if they sit next to the fruit, so you get a nice mix of textures from one handful to the next. There is no added salt, which lets the fruit do the talking.

This one is lovely stirred into plain yoghurt, scattered over a smoothie bowl, or packed into a lunchbox for a sweeter afternoon snack. It also makes a cheerful base for homemade granola bars if you chop everything a little finer.
Dried fruit can clump in warm weather, so give the bag a shake before you pour. The pieces separate easily and the flavour is unchanged.
ingredients: Raw cashews, raw almonds, dried mango, dried pineapple, banana chips (banana, sunflower oil, sugar).
mayContain: May contain traces of other tree nuts, peanuts and sulphites.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed container, away from heat so the fruit stays soft.
